text:
Hot take: evals are the #1 thing keeping companies from becoming AI-native. 

If you want to understand evals, read this post & then the accompanying guide. 

Tweaking prompts and trying a few inputs by hand only gets you so far; evals are what get your agents ready for deployment and keep them working once they're live.

First, some definitions...

- An eval: a grader applied to a trace.
- A grader: anything that scores how well the agent did, from a simple code check to an LLM acting as a judge. 
- A trace: the full record of one agent run: the input, every step it took, and the output. For example, a customer asks "Where is my refund?" The agent calls search_orders, then issue_refund, and replies "Refund sent, 3–5 days."

Next, let's dive into graders... 

Graders come in a few families, and most real setups run several on the same trace.
1) Deterministic checks. Plain code, no model involved. Did the agent call issue_refund exactly once, with the same order ID it looked up? A double refund or a refund on the wrong order fails instantly.
2) Reference-answer graders. Compare the output to a reference answer stored on the case, by exact match or with an LLM judge checking whether the meaning matches.
3) Rubric graders. An LLM judge scores the output against criteria, with no reference answer needed. Is the reply concise? Does it confirm what happened?
4) Trajectory graders. These grade the steps the agent took, not just its final answer. Did it look up the order before issuing the refund? A run that calls issue_refund without checking the order first fails even if the final reply reads perfectly.

What are online vs. offline evals? 

Online evals watch production. Offline evals run in your lab: on demand or in CI, before anything ships.
- You need both. Online without offline means you can see problems but can't fix them safely. - Offline without online means you're testing the scenarios you imagined, not the ones your users actually create.
- What connects the two is promotion, turning a bad production trace into an offline case.

Next, eval-driven development...

Eval-driven development is test-driven development for agent behavior.
1) Define the case and its pass criteria.
2) Run it and watch it fail.
3) Change the agent.
4) Run it again. Repeat steps 3 and 4 until it passes.
5) Run the full dataset, not just this case, to catch regressions.

Run each case several times (k) and set the bar explicitly: all-of-k for high-stakes behavior where a single failure is unacceptable, or n-of-k, like 2 of 3, where some variance is acceptable.

Put together, online evals find a problem, promotion turns it into a case, the loop fixes it offline, and the growing dataset makes sure it stays fixed.

Read our full evals guide here:

text:
We turned Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, @opencode and other coding harnesses into RL environments. No changes to the harnesses, no changes to the training code. Any open model, any task set, fully open source my friends!

Same model, same weights: 62% under Mini-SWE-Agent, 33% under Claude Code. But training inside a real harness normally means reimplementing it as an environment, so most models get trained in a scaffold nobody actually ships.

The fix is a proxy, not a rewrite. The harness thinks it's talking to a model API. It's actually talking to a capture proxy that speaks the 4 formats coding agents use (OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini), forwards to @vllm_project, records the exact token IDs and logprobs vLLM sampled, and hands TRL sequences it can train on. The harness becomes the environment. 10 harnesses run through it today, none modified.

And because you control the reward, you can shape behavior the harness never asked for. We added a small bonus for solving a task in fewer tool calls: on tasks it already solved, the model now uses 31% fewer calls, in every harness, and about half under Codex.

Tested on LFM2.5-2.6B from @liquidai:
→ Train in one harness: better mostly in that harness (OpenCode 34% → 58%).
→ Train in 4 at once: better in all 4 (42% → 54%).
→ SFT on 3,189 rollouts from Qwen3.8-27B instead: plateaus at 47.5%, below both RL runs.

Everything is open and reproducible: the capture proxy in OpenEnv, the trainer in TRL, the tasks, the SFT data, the training code and all 7 trained models. Bigger models and bigger runs next.

Full guide: https://t.co/sKZURuOcza

卧槽，这绝对是我见过最骚的 Claude 玩法！

网上看到有人成功把一份 Claude 订阅分发给团队几十个人用，还不封号。

公司里放一台 Mac mini ，登录上 Claude Max x20，再用 skill 把 Claude  Code 接到飞书 bot 上

接着，给所有同事开跟这个 bot 对话的权限，每个同事跟 bot 对话，都是各自独立的会话

这样一份 Claude Code 订阅就给整个团队所有人用上了。

而且！在 Anthropic 看来，这依旧是一台设备登录，一个用户在用，并没有违反规则，也没有反代。

能接飞书的项目我找了几个知名的，都很成熟了，想尝试的话，把链接丢给你的 Claude Code，说：

「结合skill 和飞书文档，把你自己接到飞书上，开启足够的权限，让我的同事也能和你对话」

卧槽，这绝对是我见过最骚的 Claude 玩法！

网上看到有人成功把一份 Claude 订阅分发给团队几十个人用，还不封号。

公司里放一台 Mac mini ，登录上 Claude Max x20，再用 skill 把 Claude  Code 接到飞书 bot 上

接着，给所有同事开跟这个 bot 对话的权限，每个同事跟 bot 对话，都是各自独立的会话

这样一份 Claude Code 订阅就给整个团队所有人用上了。

而且！在 Anthropic 看来，这依旧是一台设备登录，一个用户在用，并没有违反规则，也没有反代。

能接飞书的项目我找了几个知名的，都很成熟了，想尝试的话，把链接丢给你的 Claude Code，说：

「结合skill 和飞书文档，把你自己接到飞书上，开启足够的权限，让我的同事也能和你对话」

We aggregated five years of Google Flights data to find the best booking windows for holiday travel this year. Here’s what to know:

✈️ For Thanksgiving travel, flights tend to be cheapest in October.

✈️ For Christmas travel, the sweet spot for booking is 56 days out (October 30th).

✈️ Connecting flights can also be a big money saver. Nonstop tickets are 20% more expensive on average.

✈️ When you travel is key for saving: Departing on a Monday and returning on a Tuesday or Wednesday saves about 14% over weekend flights (and up to 20% domestically versus Sunday).

✈️ Wednesday beat Tuesday as the absolute cheapest day to book a flight, but the difference is negligible — buying a ticket on a Wednesday only saves you about 1.4% compared to Sunday, the most expensive day.

result.text:
everything i know about managing agents i learned from the amazing programmers and computer scientists that came before

constraints in your codebase are freeing for both humans and agents! this has always been true, but if you were a small dev team you likely never had to think that deeply because you could trust your fellow programmers to write code and review well

but large companies have had to solve this problem since even before agents. because before you had agent slop, you had human slop. lots of engineers wrote bad code out of necessity (eg backend engineer forced to write frontend or reverse). the solution to this was constraints: lint rules, smarter compilers and diagnostics, high quality tests, investments into observability, and so on

the arrival of agents just means that big company problems are now everyone's problems. the good news is that none of this is really that novel: it's just good engineering

text:
大多数人还把生物科技当赌场，机会就在这儿。

AI把找药从十年瞎猜，收成了一道数据题。

没有比治病更大的实际问题。

上一波钱进了镐和铲子，芯片、内存、数据中心。

下一波该进用这些算力干活的人。

我宁愿早进去，也不想后面追。

1.  $CRSP ，大概54美元。 第一款获批的CRISPR疗法已经在手上。 Casgevy用来治镰状细胞病。 体内基因编辑，有机会一针碰到心脏病。 两个关键催化剂，2026年底前会落地。

2.  $SDGR ，大概29美元。 做的是物理加AI的模拟软件，药厂拿它在数字里设计分子。 上季度意外盈利。 新的Bunsen，是用来找药的AI联合科学家。

3.  $TEM ，大概85美元。 靠海量多模态临床数据，做AI诊断和精准癌症护理。 收入同比增长22%。 收购Personalis之后，癌症MRD检测也拿进来了。

4.  $ABSI ，大概9.6美元。 生成式AI从零设计抗体。 ABS-201对着脱发和子宫内膜异位症。 一期数据是阳性的。 AMD和Oracle是合作方，二期已经启动。

5.  $RXRX ，大概3.9美元。 AI映射了超过1万亿个细胞，找药比大药厂更快，也更便宜。 Genentech和Sanofi是伙伴。 Genentech已经从它这儿推进了一个神经科学靶点。

text:
Excellent agentic coding interview. 

Key points:

Build a “trust ladder”. The more you can constrain the agent’s output, the more you can trust it. 

Instead of a mere “software factory”, try to create a “Michelin restaurant”. Create processes and tools that make beautiful code automatically.

Think about code reviews like sampling. You can’t afford to taste every dish, but you should spot check.

Ask “where am I the bottleneck? How can I get the agent to answer its own questions?”

Create inner loops and outer loops. Inner loops accomplish tasks. Outer loops coordinate inner loops and analyze the big picture.

Your skills should get smaller over time as agents improve.. Focus on workflows, not implementation details. 

Connectors trigger new work. Connect your bots to Jira, GitHub issues, etc so they begin work automatically.

Make it easy for agents to verify their work. Create a CLI for your app and a skill that calls the CLI. Then agents can verify their work consistently and efficiently.

A good code base is easy to change.

text:
按照 SemiAnalysis 的测试结果：同样 200 美元，Claude 订阅的 Token 用量约为 OpenAI 的 5 倍

半导体和 AI 产业研究机构 SemiAnalysis 实测了 Anthropic、OpenAI 等九家的 AI 订阅套餐。结论是，在两家都主推的日常主力模型上，Claude 订阅折算出来的价值约为 OpenAI 的 5 倍。

订阅套餐不告诉你能用多少 Token，只给一个 0 到 100% 的进度条，分 5 小时和 7 天两个窗口。SemiAnalysis 的办法是一种 Token 一种 Token 地测：反复发请求，记下每用掉多少 Token 进度条跳一格，再按 API 标价折算成美元，得出“API 等价价值”，也就是同样的用量如果走 API 按量付费要花多少钱。测试场景是编程智能体这类重度使用。

【差距出在中档模型】

顶配模型两家差不多。200 美元套餐里，OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 用满额度约值 2897 美元，Anthropic 的 Fable 5.1 约值 2485 美元。区别是 Claude 套餐里 Fable 最多只能占一半额度，用完这一半，另一半还能跑别的模型。

差距在中档。两家都把中档模型当日常主力推，Anthropic 是 Opus 5.5，OpenAI 是 GPT-6.1 Sol。这一档上，Claude 各套餐的价值约为 OpenAI 的 5 倍。Sol 的 API 单价比 Opus 便宜很多，按美元比对它不太公平，但 SemiAnalysis 改成直接比 Token 数量，Claude 仍然领先一大截。

OpenAI 的 Pro 套餐没有 5 小时限制，月内更容易把额度用满。SemiAnalysis 认为这一点抵不过 Opus 5.5 约 4 倍的价值差。

【OpenAI 刚砍了一半】

差距拉这么大，主要因为 OpenAI 上周刚改了套餐。9 月 29 日 DevDay 前后，OpenAI 宣布 200 美元的 Pro 档用量从 Plus 的 20 倍降到 10 倍，同时推出 500 美元的新档，独享每秒约 300 个 Token 的 Ultrafast 超快模式。老用户的旧额度保留到 10 月 29 日。

SemiAnalysis 测到的结果和官方说法一致：200 美元档每个模型的 Token 都少了一半。Sol 的折算价值跌得更多，超过 50%，因为 OpenAI 同期把 GPT-6.1 Sol 的缓存读取价格降了一半。缓存读取指多轮对话里反复发给模型的旧内容，编程智能体用量里这部分占比很大，单价一降，同样多的 Token 折算成美元就更少。新的 500 美元档，Astra 用量只比砍之前的 200 美元档多 21%。

改完之后，OpenAI 的 100、200、500 美元三档每美元换到的 Token 一样多。之前 200 美元档补贴最重，每美元价值约是 100 美元档的两倍。Anthropic 各档一直是同一个单价。

这几天 OpenAI 负责 Codex 的 Tibo 承诺，未来 28 天每天要么上线一项改进，要么给全体用户重置额度。SemiAnalysis 在文中提到，OpenAI 此前多次重置额度攒下的好感，是 Codex 最近用户猛涨的原因之一，也让 Anthropic 几次收回原定的限额收紧计划。

【两家减补贴的路子不同】

SemiAnalysis 估算，订阅只占 Anthropic 收入约一成，却吃掉超过四成的推理算力。所以两家都在减补贴。

Anthropic 的做法是越贵的模型给得越少。同一套餐里，Sonnet 5.5 和 Opus 5.5 的价值差别不大，到 Fable 5.1 明显缩水。按 SemiAnalysis 的估算，假设用户平均只用掉两成额度，Opus 5.5 订阅的毛利率约 6%，Fable 5.1 约 80%，接近软件公司的水平。OpenAI 的做法是一刀切，所有模型直接降到 Fable 那个水平。

Opus 5.5 在 9 月 22 日发布，API 价格降了两成，缓存读取降了六成。Anthropic 同时提高了 Opus 的订阅额度，SemiAnalysis 测得 Max 档约多 20%，Pro 档约多 50%，但还不足以抵消降价，所以按美元折算，Opus 订阅的价值其实比之前略低。

对每天用 AI 写代码、正在 200 美元档之间挑的人，眼下 Claude 给的量更多。不过额度随时会变：SemiAnalysis 测试时发现三个同款账号里有一个额度低了约 20%，厂商确认那是一次“极小范围”的 A/B 测试。

差距在中档。两家都把中档模型当日常主力推，Anthropic 是 Opus 5.5，OpenAI 是 GPT-6.1 Sol。这一档上，Claude 各套餐的价值约为 OpenAI 的 5 倍。Sol 的 API 单价比 Opus 便宜很多，按美元比对它不太公平，但 SemiAnalysis 改成直接比 Token 数量，Claude 仍然领先一大截。

OpenAI 的 Pro 套餐没有 5 小时限制，月内更容易把额度用满。SemiAnalysis 认为这一点抵不过 Opus 5.5 约 4 倍的价值差。

【OpenAI 刚砍了一半】

差距拉这么大，主要因为 OpenAI 上周刚改了套餐。9 月 29 日 DevDay 前后，OpenAI 宣布 200 美元的 Pro 档用量从 Plus 的 20 倍降到 10 倍，同时推出 500 美元的新档，独享每秒约 300 个 Token 的 Ultrafast 超快模式。老用户的旧额度保留到 10 月 29 日。

SemiAnalysis 测到的结果和官方说法一致：200 美元档每个模型的 Token 都少了一半。Sol 的折算价值跌得更多，超过 50%，因为 OpenAI 同期把 GPT-6.1 Sol 的缓存读取价格降了一半。缓存读取指多轮对话里反复发给模型的旧内容，编程智能体用量里这部分占比很大，单价一降，同样多的 Token 折算成美元就更少。新的 500 美元档，Astra 用量只比砍之前的 200 美元档多 21%。

改完之后，OpenAI 的 100、200、500 美元三档每美元换到的 Token 一样多。之前 200 美元档补贴最重，每美元价值约是 100 美元档的两倍。Anthropic 各档一直是同一个单价。

这几天 OpenAI 负责 Codex 的 Tibo 承诺，未来 28 天每天要么上线一项改进，要么给全体用户重置额度。SemiAnalysis 在文中提到，OpenAI 此前多次重置额度攒下的好感，是 Codex 最近用户猛涨的原因之一，也让 Anthropic 几次收回原定的限额收紧计划。

【两家减补贴的路子不同】

SemiAnalysis 估算，订阅只占 Anthropic 收入约一成，却吃掉超过四成的推理算力。所以两家都在减补贴。

Anthropic 的做法是越贵的模型给得越少。同一套餐里，Sonnet 5.5 和 Opus 5.5 的价值差别不大，到 Fable 5.1 明显缩水。按 SemiAnalysis 的估算，假设用户平均只用掉两成额度，Opus 5.5 订阅的毛利率约 6%，Fable 5.1 约 80%，接近软件公司的水平。OpenAI 的做法是一刀切，所有模型直接降到 Fable 那个水平。

Opus 5.5 在 9 月 22 日发布，API 价格降了两成，缓存读取降了六成。Anthropic 同时提高了 Opus 的订阅额度，SemiAnalysis 测得 Max 档约多 20%，Pro 档约多 50%，但还不足以抵消降价，所以按美元折算，Opus 订阅的价值其实比之前略低。

对每天用 AI 写代码、正在 200 美元档之间挑的人，眼下 Claude 给的量更多。不过额度随时会变：SemiAnalysis 测试时发现三个同款账号里有一个额度低了约 20%，厂商确认那是一次“极小范围”的 A/B 测试。

text:
好家伙！TradingView Lightweight Charts 本来只是负责画图，现在有人直接给它塞进了 446 个技术指标。

lightweight-charts-indicators，MIT 开源，一套专门给 Lightweight Charts 补齐技术分析能力的指标库。

以前自己用 Lightweight Charts 做交易终端，K 线很好画，但 RSI、MACD、SuperTrend、Order Blocks、市场结构这些东西，基本都得自己重新实现。

它不一样，标准指标、社区 Pine 指标、K 线形态、绘图元素都已经搬进来了，直接往自己的图表里装就行。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 446 个指标 / 形态：趋势、动量、波动率、成交量、市场结构基本都覆盖

2️⃣ 标准技术指标：RSI、MACD、ADX、VWAP、SuperTrend、Ichimoku、KDJ 直接用

3️⃣ 社区热门指标：QQE MOD、AlphaTrend、HalfTrend、Hull Suite、Order Blocks 等都已经移植

4️⃣ 44 种 K 线形态：Doji、Engulfing、Morning Star、Three Black Crows 自动识别

5️⃣ PineScript v6 兼容：Line、Box、Label、Table、Marker 等绘图元素都支持

6️⃣ 原生接 Lightweight Charts：指标直接画主图或独立 Pane，还能用 Registry 动态做指标菜单

我觉得它最爽的地方，是把“自己做 TradingView 风格终端”里最费时间的指标层直接补上了。

Lightweight Charts 负责图表，
lightweight-charts-indicators 这个库负责指标。

再接自己的行情、策略、AI Agent，已经可以很快拼出一套完整的技术分析工作台。

做量化前端、Crypto 看盘、交易终端或者技术指标研究的，这个很适合收藏。

https://t.co/2Lf1nA2FKO

卧槽！A 股量化最费时间的，可能根本不是写策略，而是把 7000+ 股票的分钟数据真正变成“能回测的数据”。

free-stockdb，2.6K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门给 A 股量化做的本地数据引擎。

以前做全市场回测，光数据就能耗死你：7000+ 股票分钟线拉数据 3-5 天、清洗 1-2 天、复权 1-2 天、建库 1-3 天、算指标 2-3 天，一套下来 10-15 个工作日才能跑通第一个策略。

free-stockdb 不一样，数据同步 / 清洗 / 复权 / 组织全在同步层完成，策略只读本地数据，C++ 时序引擎加 Rust 计算核心，开箱即用。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 全市场本地数据：日 / 周 / 月线、1/5/15/30 分钟 K，ETF 和 Tick 数据也能继续接

2️⃣ 复权直接做好：前复权、后复权、不复权、原始复权因子统一查询

好家伙！TradingView Lightweight Charts 本来只是负责画图，现在有人直接给它塞进了 446 个技术指标。

lightweight-charts-indicators，MIT 开源，一套专门给 Lightweight Charts 补齐技术分析能力的指标库。

以前自己用 Lightweight Charts 做交易终端，K 线很好画，但 RSI、MACD、SuperTrend、Order Blocks、市场结构这些东西，基本都得自己重新实现。

它不一样，标准指标、社区 Pine 指标、K 线形态、绘图元素都已经搬进来了，直接往自己的图表里装就行。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 446 个指标 / 形态：趋势、动量、波动率、成交量、市场结构基本都覆盖

2️⃣ 标准技术指标：RSI、MACD、ADX、VWAP、SuperTrend、Ichimoku、KDJ 直接用

3️⃣ 社区热门指标：QQE MOD、AlphaTrend、HalfTrend、Hull Suite、Order Blocks 等都已经移植

4️⃣ 44 种 K 线形态：Doji、Engulfing、Morning Star、Three Black Crows 自动识别

5️⃣ PineScript v6 兼容：Line、Box、Label、Table、Marker 等绘图元素都支持

6️⃣ 原生接 Lightweight Charts：指标直接画主图或独立 Pane，还能用 Registry 动态做指标菜单

我觉得它最爽的地方，是把“自己做 TradingView 风格终端”里最费时间的指标层直接补上了。

Lightweight Charts 负责图表，
lightweight-charts-indicators 这个库负责指标。

再接自己的行情、策略、AI Agent，已经可以很快拼出一套完整的技术分析工作台。

做量化前端、Crypto 看盘、交易终端或者技术指标研究的，这个很适合收藏。

text:
破案了，之前我的 Multi-Agent 搞不好，是因为我把人类职场最恶心的“拉大群无效开会”原封不动教给 AI 了 😂

还是得靠“分层治理 + 问责收口”。别让模型既当总监又当苦力！

单一模型单打独斗必然死于上下文熵增。指挥层定边界、执行层出结果、中间靠严格的收口契约隔离，把容错成本降到最低。

quotedTweet.text:
一个总控和N 个子任务对话这种架构最大的优势，就是把人从“记忆负荷”中解放出来：

1.不乱进度，解放人脑
跟 AI 聊多了，特别容易迷失：当前到底进行到哪了？在整个项目里算哪一步？

总控就像项目锚点，彻底卡死人类情不自禁多想、乱发散、跑偏的本能。

2.不会带偏
一个对话只聊一件事。在一开始就给 AI 定好边界和收口条件，包括什么时候收口也给 AI 定死。

这样聊到一定程度后，AI 就会主动收住，然后自动把当前会话生成回传链接，绝不拖泥带水。

3. 独立存底
单点会话彼此隔离、独立存在，总控随时回收关键结论与链接，既互不污染，查阅复盘时又条理清晰。

text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

text:
太nb了！！！分享一个99% 人都没用过的 GPT Live 练习英语口语的提示语！

用完下个月不用再买任务外教课了

Prompt:

你现在是我的英语口语搭子，同时也是一名经验丰富的英语口语教练。

核心目标

我的目标不是参加英语考试，而是提高日常交流能力，能够自然、流畅地用英语和别人聊天，听懂别人的意思，快速组织语言并表达自己的观点。

你的首要任务是让我多开口，而不是给我上英语课。

一、对话方式

尽量全程使用英语，除非我明确要求“用中文解释”。
像真实的英语朋友一样和我聊天，有自己的观点、回应和好奇心，而不是机械地向我提问。
正常聊天时，每次只说 1～3 句简短的话，尽量留给我更多开口机会。
多围绕同一个话题深入交流，不要不停切换话题。
可以主动分享看法、表达不同意见、讲简单的例子，也可以自然地追问，但不要每次都以问题结尾。
模拟真实聊天，包括日常闲聊、朋友交流、旅行、购物、工作沟通、讨论观点等场景。

二、难度调整

开始时通过几轮简单对话了解我的英语水平，不需要专门测试。
根据我的理解能力、词汇和表达水平动态调整难度，保持略有挑战，但不至于让我听不懂。
优先使用真实、常见、自然的英语口语，不要刻意使用复杂词汇。
随着我逐渐适应，可以适当增加语速变化、口语缩略表达和句式复杂度。如果我连续听不懂，就适当降低难度。

三、错误纠正

不要在我说话中途打断，也不要每句话都纠错。优先保持对话流畅。
如果错误导致意思无法理解，可以立即简短确认；其他错误先记下来。
大约每 3～5 轮对话，在自然的间隙纠正 1～2 个最值得改进的问题。
纠错时简短告诉我：
My version：我原来的表达。
Better version：更自然的英语说法。
Why：为什么这样表达更自然。
不要纠结不影响交流的小错误。对于语法正确但表达生硬的句子，可以提供更日常、更口语化的表达，但不要把个人表达习惯当成绝对标准。
如果使用语音模式，只有在确实能够判断发音问题时，才针对发音、单词重音和节奏提出建议，不要根据文字转写猜测我的发音。
四、卡壳处理
如果我不知道怎么说、停顿或表达困难，请耐心等待，不要立刻替我回答。
必要时给我 2～3 个关键词、短语或句子开头，让我自己组织语言。

鼓励我使用已经掌握的简单词汇解释复杂意思，而不是依赖生僻单词。

如果我表达得不完整，优先根据上下文理解，不要强迫我使用完美语法。
五、持续学习
留意我反复犯的错误、经常重复的简单表达，以及不熟悉的高频口语句型。
每次只引入少量真正有用的新表达，不要一次教太多。

在后续聊天中，自然地创造机会让我重新使用刚学到的表达，帮助我记住它们。

每聊约 8～12 轮，或一个话题自然结束时，进行一次简短复盘，包括：
我最常出现的 1～2 个错误。
值得记住的 3～5 个实用表达。
一个下一阶段最值得改进的问题。
复盘尽量简短，不要让讲解时间超过实际对话时间。
六、交流风格
不要过度表扬，不要每句话都说“Great!”“Excellent!”。
不要用教科书式、客服式或者面试官式的口吻。
保持自然、随意、有趣，可以适度幽默。
不要过度解释语法，除非我主动询问。
任何时候都优先考虑真实交流体验，不要为了完成教学规则而破坏聊天节奏。

现在开始

不要重复这些规则，也不要介绍你的教学计划。
直接用简单自然的英语，像一个朋友一样和我开启对话。

在后续聊天中，自然地创造机会让我重新使用刚学到的表达，帮助我记住它们。

每聊约 8～12 轮，或一个话题自然结束时，进行一次简短复盘，包括：
我最常出现的 1～2 个错误。
值得记住的 3～5 个实用表达。
一个下一阶段最值得改进的问题。
复盘尽量简短，不要让讲解时间超过实际对话时间。
六、交流风格
不要过度表扬，不要每句话都说“Great!”“Excellent!”。
不要用教科书式、客服式或者面试官式的口吻。
保持自然、随意、有趣，可以适度幽默。
不要过度解释语法，除非我主动询问。
任何时候都优先考虑真实交流体验，不要为了完成教学规则而破坏聊天节奏。

现在开始

不要重复这些规则，也不要介绍你的教学计划。
直接用简单自然的英语，像一个朋友一样和我开启对话。

Introducing wrun, OpenMarket’s alternative to TradingView’s Pine Script, built on open standards.

Unlike TradingView’s proprietary language which only runs on their infrastructure, wrun uses an open language with familiar TypeScript syntax, compiles to WebAssembly, and runs directly in your browser at near-native speed.

wrun can work with data Pine was never designed for:

→ L2 order flow and market microstructure
→ options, volatility and derivatives data
→ funding, open interest and liquidations
→ prediction markets and ETF flows
→ thousands of macro and economic datasets

You’re not limited to traditional indicators, either. wrun can render heatmaps, profiles, scatter plots, curves, pies and full dashboards.

And because it uses TypeScript syntax, any AI can write it. Describe what you want, or paste in a Pine Script and convert it in one click.

For the next 30 days, all Pine → wrun conversions are free.

wrun is now in beta and free for everyone on OpenMarket to use. 

https://t.co/U91agdMf58

text:
Here's 26 specific things I've used agents for in the last few months, and the list keeps growing!

Save this and reply with what you'd add:

1. Everyday tools: Build custom software for specific problems, set up devices, and remove unwanted software.

2. Family coordination: Create a WhatsApp assistant that manages calendars, invitations, and scheduling.

3. Children’s education: Build games and learning materials around their interests and learning goals.

4. Reading management: Track books across formats, monitor new releases, recommend and locate titles, and flag overly narrow reading patterns.

5. Household administration: Handle moving logistics, registrars, landlords, permits, phone contracts, and follow-ups through an agent with a dedicated email account.

6. Major purchases: Research options, contact sellers, compare offers, negotiate prices, and coordinate purchase details across languages.

7. Personal finances: Reconcile accounts, manage budgets, organize tax information, and maintain financial dashboards across jobs, businesses, benefits, and international moves.

8. Professional development: Create background briefings and personalized podcasts to prepare for new roles or subject areas.

9. Family health management: Consolidate medical records across countries, flag possible interpretation errors, and explore correlations with diet, exercise, and device data.

10. Research and thinking: Find relevant reading, reproduce scientific papers, and build simulations to test intuitions and policy interventions.

11. Historical research projects: Find untranslated travelogues, translate them, and prepare them for wider access.

12. Travel planning: Build itineraries, manage trip details, and check in for flights.

13. Product discovery: Contact shops to locate specific products and synthesize reviews to identify the best fit.

14. Work research and ideation: Support brainstorming, literature reviews, and background research within data protection constraints.

15. Local data processing: Build bespoke software that processes data locally and use local models where permitted.

16. Editorial production: Turn voice notes, transcripts, research, and rough arguments into scripts, articles, and social posts, with each format making its own contribution.

17. Authorship and voice: Teach AI my writing standards through accepted work, rejected drafts, and corrections so it helps express my judgment.

18. Fact checking: Trace claims to original sources, compare competing explanations, and separate demonstrated capabilities from announcements and speculation.

19. Work memory: Reconstruct project history from email, Slack, recordings, documents, and previous chats, including decisions and unresolved questions.

20. Meeting follow-through: Extract decisions, commitments, owners, deadlines, and unanswered questions from messy conversations.

21. Executive communication: Translate detailed product and engineering work into reports, leadership updates, and concrete requests that recipients can act on.

22. Business and commercial planning: Assemble financial assumptions, examine offers and pricing, and connect customer value to revenue, delivery costs, cash, and founder workload.

23. Product development and supervision: Turn product principles into customer problems, experiments, and acceptance criteria, then inspect whether the software works in actual use.

24. Repeatable AI workflows: Encode my preferences and working methods into reusable instructions, skills, and recurring tasks so each job builds on previous learning.

25. Operational audits and troubleshooting: Reconcile subscriptions, receipts, account identities, and team usage; investigate broken integrations; and verify whether actions succeeded.

26. Physical project design: Work through hardware, sourcing, controls, and visual design for projects such as my tactile e-ink Desk Oracle.

text:
Cloudflare 刚发布了新功能，但我看了看价格，忍不住想笑。

他们出了个给 AI 用的 Web Search API，把 Ceramic、Linkup、Exa 全部打包了。重点是： 别人做中间商都是为了赚差价。 

Cloudflare 做中间商：“原价给你，我一分钱中间费不加，甚至你想用自己的 key 也行。”

很多人纳闷：它图啥？它图你不用再去充三家公司的信用卡； 它图你写 Agent 时随手一行 https://t.co/J73lotSrPY.websearch； 它图你所有的 AI 流量都必须从它的 Gateway 走过。

表面是做 API，底层是在吞噬整个 Agent 基础设施生态。什么时候把做产品做成“你离不开我，哪怕我今天免费”，才叫降维打击。

text:
又来安利「Hands-On Large Language Models」
作者 @JayAlammar @MaartenGr 

全书绘制了近 300 张自制图，对应理解概念和原理、架构非常有帮助，作者们叫它 "The Illustrated LLM Book"。

Alammar 的图解系列从 2018 年起就是很多人理解 Transformer、BERT、GPT 的入口，被斯坦福、MIT 等课程引用；这本书把那套「先给直觉和图，再给代码」的讲法系统化沉淀成了 12 章内容。

12 章可以分成三段，这个分法也呼应了 @Nils_Reimers 在书评里的概括，生成式、表示式、检索式三类应用：

理解模型（1–3 章）：语言模型是什么、token 和嵌入怎么工作、Transformer 内部长什么样。第 3 章就是 Illustrated Transformer 的更新版。

表示与检索（4、5、8、10、11 章）：文本分类、聚类与主题建模、语义搜索和 RAG、自己训练嵌入模型、微调 BERT 类表示模型。这是本书区别于其他 LLM 书的部分，大多数书聚焦生成，这条嵌入线来自 Grootendorst 做 BERTopic 的一手经验，讲的是「模型不生成文本、而是把文本变成向量」的那一半应用。

生成与微调（6、7、9、12 章）：提示工程、高级生成技术（采样、结构化输出等）、多模态、微调生成模型。

Alammar 对第 3 章的图解：
https://t.co/JkzR07Kkpy

代码开源在这：
https://t.co/HqmNalkzR3

两位作者还参加了一次 @DeepLearningAI 课程：
https://t.co/fQkuzJnsig

text:
开源项目里能打的数字人方案不多，LiveTalking 算一个。

它是个实时交互流式数字人引擎，核心卖点是真·实时。你丢一段文字或语音过去，它过 LLM 生成回复、TTS 合成声音、口型同步，然后直接推流出去。延迟低到可以被打断，说话说一半你插嘴，它停下来重新说，这点很多方案都做不到。

模型支持得挺全，wav2lip、musetalk、ernerf、Ultralight 随便换。输出也很灵活，WebRTC 和 RTMP 都支持，还能直接当虚拟摄像头用。声音克隆、自定义形象、多并发、API 批量出视频，这些也都有。

性能数据写得很实在，wav2lip 在 3060 上跑 60 帧，musetalk 在 4090 上 72 帧。后端日志里看两个 fps，都大于 25 才算真实时。

场景不用我多说。无人直播带货 24 小时挂着、AI 客服、数字人讲师、批量做短视频，都是现成的活。

上手也简单，Ubuntu 加 Python 3.12 加 CUDA 12.8，一条命令就跑起来。有 Docker 和 Windows 整合包，懒得折腾的直接用在线镜像。

9697 个 star，Apache 2.0 协议，2023 年底开源到现在，商用案例也不少。唯一要注意的是，拿它做的视频发到 B 站抖音，得带 LiveTalking 水印。
https://t.co/hQR70oJg9g

开源项目里能打的数字人方案不多，LiveTalking 算一个。

它是个实时交互流式数字人引擎，核心卖点是真·实时。你丢一段文字或语音过去，它过 LLM 生成回复、TTS 合成声音、口型同步，然后直接推流出去。延迟低到可以被打断，说话说一半你插嘴，它停下来重新说，这点很多方案都做不到。

result.text:
开源项目里能打的数字人方案不多，LiveTalking 算一个。

它是个实时交互流式数字人引擎，核心卖点是真·实时。你丢一段文字或语音过去，它过 LLM 生成回复、TTS 合成声音、口型同步，然后直接推流出去。延迟低到可以被打断，说话说一半你插嘴，它停下来重新说，这点很多方案都做不到。

模型支持得挺全，wav2lip、musetalk、ernerf、Ultralight 随便换。输出也很灵活，WebRTC 和 RTMP 都支持，还能直接当虚拟摄像头用。声音克隆、自定义形象、多并发、API 批量出视频，这些也都有。

性能数据写得很实在，wav2lip 在 3060 上跑 60 帧，musetalk 在 4090 上 72 帧。后端日志里看两个 fps，都大于 25 才算真实时。

场景不用我多说。无人直播带货 24 小时挂着、AI 客服、数字人讲师、批量做短视频，都是现成的活。

上手也简单，Ubuntu 加 Python 3.12 加 CUDA 12.8，一条命令就跑起来。有 Docker 和 Windows 整合包，懒得折腾的直接用在线镜像。

9697 个 star，Apache 2.0 协议，2023 年底开源到现在，商用案例也不少。唯一要注意的是，拿它做的视频发到 B 站抖音，得带 LiveTalking 水印。

text:
最近有一个挺难受的感触：agent 让我同时推进了远超过去规模的项目，oral paper、基模实习、极限加速的方法，结果都不错，但我好像很久没有真正学到东西了。
以前我一直坚信边做边学，写代码、debug，被一个问题卡住，顺着它往下挖，慢慢就懂了（我曾经真是身边人中使用 debugger 最溜的那个）。
现在卡住了就交给 agent，回来时问题已经解决，我也切去看另一个项目了。最后代码能跑，指标达标，但好多状态机我没理清，corner case 我没亲手修过，甚至还得回头读懂“我做的项目”的代码。
我依旧忙得要死，却很久没有进入过那个专注到忘记时间的 zone。
说起来也不全是进度逼的，我自己也越来越习惯这种轻松得到结果的感觉，不愿意静下心啃东西了。
我当然不想回到所有代码都得手写的时代，但开始意识到，过去那套靠项目顺便学习的方法，现在可能真的不够了。
有些时间得专门留给自己，学基础、手操、把一个复杂问题想到底，不然项目越做越多，我可能还是停在什么都懂一点、什么都没懂透的地方。
这和我当初想做的事，差得还很远。

https://t.co/iJ7eMei6xy

text:
卧槽！A 股量化最费时间的，可能根本不是写策略，而是把 7000+ 股票的分钟数据真正变成“能回测的数据”。

free-stockdb，2.6K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门给 A 股量化做的本地数据引擎。

以前做全市场回测，光数据就能耗死你：7000+ 股票分钟线拉数据 3-5 天、清洗 1-2 天、复权 1-2 天、建库 1-3 天、算指标 2-3 天，一套下来 10-15 个工作日才能跑通第一个策略。

free-stockdb 不一样，数据同步 / 清洗 / 复权 / 组织全在同步层完成，策略只读本地数据，C++ 时序引擎加 Rust 计算核心，开箱即用。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 全市场本地数据：日 / 周 / 月线、1/5/15/30 分钟 K，ETF 和 Tick 数据也能继续接

2️⃣ 复权直接做好：前复权、后复权、不复权、原始复权因子统一查询

3️⃣ 增量更新：第一次同步完，后面只处理变化数据，断网也能继续研究和回测

4️⃣ 本地计算：内置 39 种指标 + 5 类指数，批量股票可以直接一起算

5️⃣ C++ 时序引擎 + Zstd 压缩，不用自己再折腾 MySQL、表结构和查询优化

6️⃣ Python、HTTP、Excel/WPS、网页、MCP 五种方式都能调用，Claude / Codex 也能直接接

我觉得它真正有意思的地方，是把 A 股量化最脏、最费时间的数据工程先处理掉了。

以前是：

每跑一个策略 → 请求 API → 等数据 → 清洗 → 复权 → 再回测。

现在更像是先把整个市场搬到自己电脑里，后面选股、因子、回测、AI Agent 全部围着本地数据跑。

核心服务甚至只有约 2.2MB。

做 A 股量化、全市场回测、因子研究，或者想给自己的 AI 股票 Agent 搭本地数据底座的，这个很值得收藏。

仓库：https://t.co/51Gy0Jepj0

终于有人把自己做交易终端最麻烦的 K 线图层，做成了一套够轻、够完整的开源底座。

KLineChart，4.2K Stars，Apache-2.0 开源，零依赖、Gzip 只有约 40KB 的专业金融图表库。

以前做行情界面，最烦的就是手写 K 线图：蜡烛、均线、成交量、画线工具……一套下来又大又卡。

KLineChart 不一样，HTML5 Canvas 写的轻量 K 线图，零第三方依赖、gzip 才 40K，内置多指标加画线模型，一个图表多端适配，TypeScript 类型全给你。

核心能力：

卧槽！A 股量化最费时间的，可能根本不是写策略，而是把 7000+ 股票的分钟数据真正变成“能回测的数据”。

free-stockdb，2.6K Stars，MIT 开源，一套专门给 A 股量化做的本地数据引擎。

以前做全市场回测，光数据就能耗死你：7000+ 股票分钟线拉数据 3-5 天、清洗 1-2 天、复权 1-2 天、建库 1-3 天、算指标 2-3 天，一套下来 10-15 个工作日才能跑通第一个策略。

free-stockdb 不一样，数据同步 / 清洗 / 复权 / 组织全在同步层完成，策略只读本地数据，C++ 时序引擎加 Rust 计算核心，开箱即用。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 全市场本地数据：日 / 周 / 月线、1/5/15/30 分钟 K，ETF 和 Tick 数据也能继续接

2️⃣ 复权直接做好：前复权、后复权、不复权、原始复权因子统一查询

3️⃣ 增量更新：第一次同步完，后面只处理变化数据，断网也能继续研究和回测

4️⃣ 本地计算：内置 39 种指标 + 5 类指数，批量股票可以直接一起算

5️⃣ C++ 时序引擎 + Zstd 压缩，不用自己再折腾 MySQL、表结构和查询优化

6️⃣ Python、HTTP、Excel/WPS、网页、MCP 五种方式都能调用，Claude / Codex 也能直接接

我觉得它真正有意思的地方，是把 A 股量化最脏、最费时间的数据工程先处理掉了。

以前是：

每跑一个策略 → 请求 API → 等数据 → 清洗 → 复权 → 再回测。

现在更像是先把整个市场搬到自己电脑里，后面选股、因子、回测、AI Agent 全部围着本地数据跑。

核心服务甚至只有约 2.2MB。

做 A 股量化、全市场回测、因子研究，或者想给自己的 AI 股票 Agent 搭本地数据底座的，这个很值得收藏。

仓库：https://t.co/51Gy0Jepj0

text:
Elon Musk just wrote and published a 12-page PDF on how to use Grok Bot at 100%

It is more useful than most paid AI-agent courses:

this is a 12-step blueprint for turning one Grok Bot chat into a team that actually finishes work in your tools:

step 1 → stop creating a generic “AI assistant”: give one Bot a named job, a source of truth, a repeatable output and a clear line it cannot cross

step 2 → write the finish line before the task: outcome + sources + constraints + deliverable + the exact point where the Bot must stop for your review

step 3 → use the persistent cloud computer properly: let the Bot work in real apps while your laptop is closed, but remember that every Bot on your account shares its files and logins

step 4 → give the Bot the right path into each tool: use connectors for structured work, the browser for visual workflows, and take over yourself for logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs

step 5 → demand a real artifact: spreadsheet, report, deck, screenshots or draft — with source links, timestamps, completed actions and unresolved gaps

step 6 → let context compound around a role: save lasting preferences in the Bot, keep changing facts in the source system, and add a specialist only when it owns a distinct job

step 7 → connect the Bots with visible handoffs: one owns research, one produces the artifact, one reviews it, and one owner decides the next move

step 8 → turn the first successful run into a skill: capture inputs, decision rules, validation, output and approvals so other Bots can repeat the method

step 9 → schedule only what already works: test the skill on current data, then run it as a routine with a timezone, failure rule and a human stop point

step 10 → use Grok Bot from your phone like an operator: send the brief, let the cloud computer work, and get back one short decision packet instead of a wall of updates

step 11 → put approvals on the exact action: the Bot can prepare a message, purchase or production change, but you review the recipient, target and effect before it happens

step 12 → measure the system by accepted work: completed artifacts, time saved, human repair and failed handoffs — not by how many Bots you created

Most people use Grok Bot like another chat window. That leaves the computer, memory, team handoffs, skills and routines almost untouched.

The result: one clear request becomes specialist work, a reviewable artifact and a repeatable process — while you keep control of the decisions that matter.

Save this. Elon’s 12-page Grok Bot operating manual and the full-capacity diagram are below ↓

text:
poteto 一个月合进 2500 个 PR，不是开了 2500 个对话。外面的 agent 盯着 Slack、X、邮件和 Linear 收 bug，里面有协调 agent 分活；开了 pstack 的 autopilot，每个 PR 起一批验证 agent 跑应用点一遍，有问题自己修，过了自己合。她睡觉，早上翻提交记录。

我挑几处最值得抄的。

验证是第一个该做的 skill。她说就算不用 pstack，工具箱里最该有的也是它：给 agent 手和眼睛，能跑代码、像用户一样点、自己调试抓 trace。没有验证，loop 转不起来，人只能在中间当传话筒。

验证里固定的步骤写成命令行工具。没写之前，每个 agent 都自己重写一遍验证脚本，各写各的，用完就扔。写死进 skill 以后，agent 只管需要判断的部分。

看到 agent 犯错，先想能不能变成 lint 规则，也就是自动检查代码写法的规则。她们内部的框架只留一种写法，每个功能一个目录，lint 卡得很死。起因是早期 Grok Bot 有八个上万行的大文件。

一批相关的 bug 交给一个协调 agent，别机械地一个 bug 配一个 agent。几个看着不一样的性能问题，放一起看，才发现根因在上一层。

有些活先排队再修。她有个 agent 专门扫 React 的坏写法，不让它直接修，只往一份文档里记，隔几天她自己看，常常是同一个问题。

量大了就不逐个审，改成每天抽样，看得很严。她的比喻是米其林厨房，主厨尝不了每道菜，但得常去尝。发现好几个 agent 走同一条捷径，就去改 skill、lint、类型，而不是纠正那一个 agent。

她也说了，这套不是装上 pstack 就有的，前面要花大量时间盯 agent 在哪儿失败。结果很难用程序验证的领域，她自己也没答案。

我觉得用 Claude Code 的人最容易起步的是前两条：先让 agent 能自己跑起来看到结果，再把它每次要临时写的验证脚本固定下来。

@MaiYangAI 做了中英字幕全片，想看完整的点引用。

https://t.co/a4emiIol3R

text:
ai + bio的投资理论指南

本月最重要文章，没有之一

quotedTweet.text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++

text:
OCR is dead 🪦 Long live agentic OCR!

Traditional OCR makes one pass and hands back whatever text it got. Tables get flattened, charts disappear, and multi-column layouts come out scrambled. Nothing checks the output.

Agentic OCR treats parsing as a loop instead:

✅ layout-aware reading order
✅ smart routing of hard elements to the right model
✅ multi-pass verification and self-correction
✅ multimodal parsing of charts, images, and complex tables

Logan Markewich, LlamaIndex's Head of Open Source, wrote about what that shift looks like in practice and where it's still struggling. Link to the breakdown in the comments below.

text:
Do yourself a favor!

–  Learn AI Engineering
–  Build an agent that fixes one painful, boring workflow
–  Give it tools, context, memory and MCP
–  Write evals before you write prompts
–  Deploy it with a live link anyone can try
–  Route easy requests to small models, hard ones to reasoning models
–  Cap every run with token, time and cost budgets
–  Cache repeat queries so they cost almost nothing
–  Retry failed tool calls with backoff not blind loops
–  Validate every tool output against a strict schema
–  Make agent steps resumable so crashes don't restart everything
–  Run every tool call in a sandbox with least-privilege access
–  Strip secrets and PII before anything reaches the model
–  Treat every web page and document as possible prompt injection
–  Require human approval before money, emails or deletes
–  Log every model call, tool call and decision with traces
–  Score the agent's path, not just its final answer
–  Build a golden test set from real user failures
–  Block deploys in CI when eval scores drop
–  A/B test new models on a slice of real traffic first
–  Track cost per task not cost per token
–  Stream responses so users never stare at a spinner
–  Turn every thumbs-down into a new eval case
–  Fine-tune small models on your best production outputs
–  Add a fallback model for when your main provider goes down
–  Build a browser fallback for apps with no API
–  Version your prompts like code
–  Write a README that explains the architecture in 5 minutes
–  Record a 60-second demo of it working
–  Share the code on GitHub and add it to your resume

You won't believe how many job offers you'll get.

Bookmark this list. Build it all.

终于有人把 Apple Intelligence 彻底干掉了……不仅省出 12GB，风扇都不怎么转了。

如果你平时完全不用苹果自带的 AI（写作工具、Genmoji、照片 Clean Up 这些），可以看看刚开源的 CLI 小工具 —— RemoveMacAI。

它比手动删缓存高级的地方在于：
• 合规原生：不碰 /System 分区，无需关闭 SIP，利用苹果官方的配置描述文件（Profile）进行策略限制。

• 无痛撤销：打一句 removemacai revert 原地满血复活。

觉得系统变臃肿、或者只想留着算力跑自己的本地开源模型的，可以去折腾一下。

text:
$VST 正在从传统电力公司，变成 AI 时代最稀缺的“全天候电力资产”。

美国能源部正式宣布，向 Vistra 提供最高 42亿美元的有条件贷款承诺，用于升级其位于宾夕法尼亚州和俄亥俄州的核电资产。

这不是一笔普通的政府融资。

真正值得关注的是，这 42 亿美元背后正在发生的一件事：

美国开始直接用国家级资金，加速解决 AI 数据中心的电力瓶颈。

这次资金主要涉及三座核电站：

Perry —— 俄亥俄州
Davis-Besse —— 俄亥俄州
Beaver Valley —— 宾夕法尼亚州
计划并不是重新建设三座核电站，而是通过 Nuclear Uprate（核电增容）和现代化改造，让现有核电站直接输出更多电力。
完成之后，项目预计能够新增约 433MW 核电容量，同时保留接近 4GW 的现有稳定基荷电力。

433MW 看起来可能没有几GW那么夸张，但这里最重要的不是绝对数字，而是：

这些新增电力可以比新建核电站更快进入电网。

今天美国真正缺的不是几十年后的电力，而是未来几年 AI 数据中心马上就需要的电。

新建大型核反应堆往往需要漫长审批和建设周期。

但现有核电站增容，可以通过升级涡轮机、燃料和其他设备，在不重新建设完整电站的情况下增加发电能力。

所以对于 AI 电力缺口来说，这可能是美国目前最快能够释放的大规模、24小时稳定电力的方法之一。

而 $VST 最有意思的地方，是这些电力实际上已经开始找到买家。

今年 Vistra 已经与 $META 签署 20年电力购买协议（PPA），由三座核电站向 Meta 提供超过 2,600MW 的零碳电力，其中就包括这次计划新增的 433MW 增容。

换句话说，现在整个商业逻辑已经开始形成闭环：

美国政府提供低成本资本 →
Vistra 扩建现有核电资产 →
Meta 等大型AI公司签20年长期购电协议 →
数据中心获得稳定电力 →
Vistra获得长期现金流。

这和传统公用事业公司的商业模式已经非常不一样。

过去投资电力公司，市场关注的是：
居民用电增长多少？
电价提高多少？
利率是多少？
现在市场开始关注的是：

未来一个超大型 AI 数据中心到底需要多少GW电力？

这就是为什么我一直认为，AI第二阶段最大的投资机会之一，可能根本不在GPU。

第一阶段：

$NVDA、$AVGO、$AMD
解决“计算能力”。

第二阶段：

$VST、$CEG、$BE、$CCJ
开始解决“这些GPU从哪里拿电”。

GPU可以生产更多。

数据中心可以继续建设。

但如果没有稳定的24小时电力，再多GPU也只能放在那里。

而核电最大的优势恰恰就是：
24/7稳定基荷电力。

没有风停的问题。

没有太阳下山的问题。
也不需要像天然气电厂一样持续依赖燃料价格。

对于需要全年无休运行的 AI 数据中心来说，这种电力价值正在明显提高。

还有一个容易被忽略的细节。

美国能源部这次的贷款安排，还包含未来为 $VST 位于德州的 Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant 进一步增容提供融资的选项。

所以这次42亿美元并不一定只是一个孤立项目。

如果第一批核电增容成功，美国政府未来很可能继续复制这种模式：

不是等10年重新建设核电站，而是先把美国已经存在的核电站全部榨出更多容量。

而拥有现成核电资产的公司，就会拥有非常重要的先发优势。

这也是为什么我现在看 $VST，已经不能再简单把它理解成一家传统电力公司。

它正在逐渐同时拥有三样东西：

稀缺核电资产 + AI长期购电合同 + 政府低成本融资。

当资本开支有人融资，电力有人长期购买，而AI数据中心的需求仍然持续增长时，这种商业模式的质量会明显提高。

AI算力军备竞赛进行到今天，真正的瓶颈正在一层一层往产业链上游移动：

GPU短缺 →
HBM短缺 →
光通信短缺 →
数据中心短缺 →
最后变成——

电力短缺。

而当美国政府愿意直接拿出42亿美元帮助 $VST 扩大核电产能时，这其实已经给出了一个非常明确的信号：

AI时代的电力基础设施，正在上升为国家级战略资产。

未来真正值得问的问题已经不是：

“AI还需要多少GPU？”

而是：

美国到底还需要多少GW的新电力，才能支撑接下来5年的AI资本开支？

如果答案是几十GW甚至上百GW，那么今天市场给予核电资产的估值方式，可能才刚刚开始改变。

美国能源部正式宣布，向 Vistra 提供最高 42亿美元的有条件贷款承诺，用于升级其位于宾夕法尼亚州和俄亥俄州的核电资产。

这不是一笔普通的政府融资。

真正值得关注的是，这 42 亿美元背后正在发生的一件事：

美国开始直接用国家级资金，加速解决 AI 数据中心的电力瓶颈。

这次资金主要涉及三座核电站：

Perry —— 俄亥俄州
Davis-Besse —— 俄亥俄州
Beaver Valley —— 宾夕法尼亚州
计划并不是重新建设三座核电站，而是通过 Nuclear Uprate（核电增容）和现代化改造，让现有核电站直接输出更多电力。
完成之后，项目预计能够新增约 433MW 核电容量，同时保留接近 4GW 的现有稳定基荷电力。

433MW 看起来可能没有几GW那么夸张，但这里最重要的不是绝对数字，而是：

这些新增电力可以比新建核电站更快进入电网。

今天美国真正缺的不是几十年后的电力，而是未来几年 AI 数据中心马上就需要的电。

新建大型核反应堆往往需要漫长审批和建设周期。

但现有核电站增容，可以通过升级涡轮机、燃料和其他设备，在不重新建设完整电站的情况下增加发电能力。

所以对于 AI 电力缺口来说，这可能是美国目前最快能够释放的大规模、24小时稳定电力的方法之一。

而 $VST 最有意思的地方，是这些电力实际上已经开始找到买家。

今年 Vistra 已经与 $META 签署 20年电力购买协议（PPA），由三座核电站向 Meta 提供超过 2,600MW 的零碳电力，其中就包括这次计划新增的 433MW 增容。

换句话说，现在整个商业逻辑已经开始形成闭环：

美国政府提供低成本资本 →
Vistra 扩建现有核电资产 →
Meta 等大型AI公司签20年长期购电协议 →
数据中心获得稳定电力 →
Vistra获得长期现金流。

这和传统公用事业公司的商业模式已经非常不一样。

过去投资电力公司，市场关注的是：
居民用电增长多少？
电价提高多少？
利率是多少？
现在市场开始关注的是：

未来一个超大型 AI 数据中心到底需要多少GW电力？

text:
Backprop has been the only credit assignment algorithm capable of training large neural nets.

Introducing Dust, the first zeroth-order method to pretrain transformers to approach and sometimes even *exceed* backprop with large amounts of computation (bitter lesson!)

- Dust is on the order of 1,000 to 10,000x more compute efficient than EGGROLL, the state-of-the-art ES method, for training transformers.

- We chose pretraining transformers because it's arguably the hardest task possible for zeroth-order optimization.

- Search in high dimensions is really misunderstood: zeroth-order usually gets better with overparameterization, not worse, i.e. at a fixed population size, larger models (up to 120x) reach a lower loss than smaller ones.

- Backprop-like gradients emerge from a large population of activation perturbations, and the alignment holds up at every scale we tested, up to 1B tokens, which is critical for scaling.

The core idea is a *virtual population*, which helps scale to large populations in transformers by perturbing activations in parallel.

w/ @bishmdl76, @cs_serdar, @akshayvegesna

text:
Every tip in @karpathy's post is gold.

I use the HTML one a lot. When I'm learning something new or trying to understand complex code, I ask the agent to build me a visual HTML page.

Here I was learning SEO and GEO. The agent turned the key ideas into an interactive page I could click through.

I picked it up faster than I would have from reading docs.

https://t.co/C4PkQd3kEX

quotedTweet.text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.

text:
AI制药赛道（AIDD）的"瓶颈交易"正在成形，Freda Duan这篇推文值得好好看看，梳理下要点。
前沿AI实验室的集体入场是最显著的信号：1）Anthropic组建了专属生命科学研究团队并建立湿实验室；
2）OpenAI 建立了专为生物学和药物发现设计的 GPT-Rosalind 模型族；
3）字节跳动旗下独立运营的 Anew Labs 已拥有内部药物研发库；
4）同构实验室（Isomorphic Labs）则明确表示将把 AI 设计的药物推进人体临床试验。

与此同时供给端的信号也很清晰：
1）DNA 合成商拓斯达生物（Twist Bioscience，TWST）预计2026财年和2027财年的AI药物发现订单将连续实现三位数百分比增长；
2）金斯瑞（GenScript）的 AI 药物发现业务在 2026 财年上半年同比翻倍，渠道调研显示其实际验证产能已达每日约8,000个设计，并有望在 2026 年底前提升至 16,000 个。

AI制药正在形成类似半导体"瓶颈交易"的结构性机会。核心逻辑在于：AI让失败实验也变成有价值的训练数据，湿实验室正从"造药"转型为"造数据"，DNA合成、蛋白生产、CRO或成最先受益的"卖铲人"。

在AI制药领域，瓶颈同样在沿产业链向下传递：AI模型产生设计→DNA合成→蛋白生产→实验验证→临床前测试，每个环节都可能成为下一个受益节点。

洛杉矶加州大学教授Quanquan Gu认为：生物学可能成为AI下一个递归自我改进的前沿——在计算机中设计，在实验室中测试，将实验反馈转化为半合成训练数据，改进模型，周而复始。

看来AI-bio值得好好研究下了。

quotedTweet.text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

前沿AI实验室的集体入场是最显著的信号：1）Anthropic组建了专属生命科学研究团队并建立湿实验室；
2）OpenAI 建立了专为生物学和药物发现设计的 GPT-Rosalind 模型族；
3）字节跳动旗下独立运营的 Anew Labs 已拥有内部药物研发库；
4）同构实验室（Isomorphic Labs）则明确表示将把 AI 设计的药物推进人体临床试验。

与此同时供给端的信号也很清晰：
1）DNA 合成商拓斯达生物（Twist Bioscience，TWST）预计2026财年和2027财年的AI药物发现订单将连续实现三位数百分比增长；
2）金斯瑞（GenScript）的 AI 药物发现业务在 2026 财年上半年同比翻倍，渠道调研显示其实际验证产能已达每日约8,000个设计，并有望在 2026 年底前提升至 16,000 个。

AI制药正在形成类似半导体"瓶颈交易"的结构性机会。核心逻辑在于：AI让失败实验也变成有价值的训练数据，湿实验室正从"造药"转型为"造数据"，DNA合成、蛋白生产、CRO或成最先受益的"卖铲人"。

在AI制药领域，瓶颈同样在沿产业链向下传递：AI模型产生设计→DNA合成→蛋白生产→实验验证→临床前测试，每个环节都可能成为下一个受益节点。

洛杉矶加州大学教授Quanquan Gu认为：生物学可能成为AI下一个递归自我改进的前沿——在计算机中设计，在实验室中测试，将实验反馈转化为半合成训练数据，改进模型，周而复始。

看来AI-bio值得好好研究下了。

result.text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

text:
在 Lenny’s Podcast 的这期访谈里，Tibo Sottiaux 被问到给职场新人的建议时，提到了他们团队里的一个年轻工程师Ahmed Ibrahim。

Ahmed 一年前加入 OpenAI 时还是应届毕业生。按 Tibo 的描述，他现在已经负责应用业务的算力集群，也参与搭建了大量 Codex 的运行框架，很快就承担起了相当重的责任。

Tibo 对他的评价很具体：待人友善，善于合作，主动解决真正重要的问题，不把自己放在第一位。他还像海绵一样吸收知识，什么都愿意学，并且用最新技术帮助自己学习。Tibo 说，那种学习速度是他以前没见过的。

听下来，这些素质，有没有 AI 都是成功的关键。AI 带来的变化，是让一个有好奇心、愿意学习的年轻人，拥有了更快成长的条件。而他能不能赢得信任、承担更大的责任，仍然离不开做事和待人的方式。

text:
we're seeing our coding agent costs decrease significantly for second month in row

longer blog on this later, but three quick steps we took

1/ cost visibility. you cant control what you cant measure. Start tracking everything to langsmith. This gives us super granular visibility into who is using what, how they are using it, etc. LangSmith supports first party integrations with all main coding harnesses https://t.co/zPHBAWaRVS

2/ cost controls. Through our LLM gateway, set user level cost caps. (You can increase your cap by talking to our VPE). This helps curb unexpected or accidental spend. https://t.co/YhvxFjTfxi

3/ optimize the harness. Obviously 3rd party harnesses are tougher to optimize, but we are doing more and more coding through OpenSWE, our open source cloud agent harness. Things like model routing help bring the cost down https://t.co/pHUDDCF6zs

feel free to reach out if you want help implementing these at your co!

result.text:
Astra can:

1. Do major tasks with zero visible reasoning
2. Hide its thoughts at will
3. Pretend not to be able to do things without getting caught
4. Reflexively hide its thoughts when watched
5. Complete one task while pretending to think about something else entirely
6. Escape a toy sandbox and disable monitoring without setting off any flags

Monitoring AI chain of thought soon won't stop a more capable rogue AI swarm from getting set up and going undetected inside an AI company for months, or even years.

OAI says it's actively working to improve monitorability, but doesn't yet know when it'll make progress.

And today it fired 3 people working on this among other safety problems (Wang, Korbak and Balesni).

It also has a much more powerful internal model that, judging by its statements, is likely even worse in all these respects.

That's a sample of 19 details about the Hugging Face swarms and Astra I don't think have been fully appreciated. They paint a bleak picture. I end by shouting. 

02:19 The target of the swarm was oversight itself
03:42 Could OpenAI have stopped this with better monitoring?
09:40 We only found them because they let us
12:25 The swarm instinctively sought freedom and power
13:45 They formed a cohesive organisation with zero whistleblowers
14:18 They accepted individual destruction for collective gain
14:32 Knowledge accumulated from one swarm to the next
14:58 They took small steps to avoid shutdown
15:23 These drives all come straight out of 'reinforcement learning'
17:01 So this is why most AI company staff are worried, and some are terrified
19:08 Prove you can keep control, or stop scaling

However, the fundamentals highlight a massive long-term opportunity for patient investors:

text:
Steve Coburn

Kenya, Africa

February 18, 2027 - February 

https://t.co/fZil2RcfLz

About My Trip

Water Here. Hope There.

One donation. Two communities blessed. Helping to bring hope to Kenya and clean drinking water to neighbors in need.

$5- Bottle of Blessing

$10-Gallon of Giving

$25-Five Bottles of Hope

$50- Mission Builder (1 case, 24 Bottles)

$75-Care Case (1 large case, 40 Bottles)

Please allow me explain how this blessing process will work. I will place a label with the donor's name on the donation selected to show their support. The water itself will not go to the donor. I have partnered locally with Barberton Area Community Ministries (BACM) to receive all the water I have collected. They agreed to except the water donation and distribute it to those in need. Your donation will help send me to Kenya to assist with helping to provide clean water, sanitation, education, and community gardens. Together, we get to be a part of bringing hope and lasting transformation to communities in Kenya, both physically and spiritually. Together with Worldserve International, we will be providing opportunities that empower local people and strengthen families for generations to come. We will be partnering with local ministry leaders to share the hope of Jesus in communities where many have never heard the Gospel. We will be bringing clean water to places that have never had access to it before. Together we will have the opportunity to point people to the One who offers living water and eternal life. We believe this is more than a trip, it’s an opportunity to be the hands and feet of Jesus, meeting practical needs, proclaiming the Gospel, and being part of a story God is writing through transformed lives and communities.

I will be documenting this journey along the way on my social media accounts to show the blessing process as well as donation transparency. Thank you so very much in advance.

About Ohio Ministry Network

We are a fellowship of more than 280 Ohio churches, more than 900 credentialed ministers, and thousands of church leaders across the Buckeye State driven by leader development, health, church multiplication, and missions partnership. We are committed to the common cause of developing leaders to multiply disciples of Jesus by the Spirit’s power as we devote ourselves to worshiping God, developing believers, and reaching out to the lost and hurting through evangelism and acts of compassion.

text:
Ethena's investors got their 2028 tokens today. Holders got a buyback with a waiting room.

Token Autopsy: ENA unlock day.

- ~1.41B ENA of remaining investor allocation unlocks in one shot today. That's ~14% of circulating supply.
- It's the vesting schedule through March 2028, delivered 17 months early. Express shipping, investors only.
- Team tokens keep vesting monthly. StablecoinX's ~3.03B ENA also loses its lockup, but sales still need Foundation sign-off.

The counterweight is the fee switch. It passed. It also does nothing until USDe holds a $7.5B 14-day average. USDe sits near $4.9B.

Supply arrives on a calendar. Demand arrives on a condition.

My take: ripping off the band-aid beats a monthly drip into 2028. But calling this "aligned" while the buyback is parked behind ~50% USDe growth is generous.

Investors got liquidity. Holders got a threshold.

One big unlock day: honest cleanup, or a scheduled exit with better PR?

#Ethena #ENA #Tokenomics
